A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A long upland valley at dusk in late autumn, seen from low on a frosted hillside of cropped turf on the valley's south side, looking down and across to the north-west. Still air, a clear cold evening, the last light going out of the sky. In the near foreground, small against the width of the valley and seen from behind and a little to one side, one figure stands on the turf looking down the slope. A tall, narrow hooded figure a little over seven feet, thin enough to look like a doorframe someone has dressed. A long coat the color of the last light on a wall: a dull amber that goes brown and then grey the longer the eye stays on it. The hood is always up. Under the hood there is no face, only a small steady flame the size of a fist, a lamp-flame with no lamp, that does not flicker in wind. The flame lights whatever stands before it and does not light the figure itself; the coat and hood stay in their own shadow. The hands are ordinary, long-fingered and a little too still. In one hand a plain iron lantern, which swings slowly as though its bearer were walking, even when the figure stands dead still. The figure does not shift its weight, turn its head quickly, or hurry. It stands at thresholds and waits. The lantern in its hand is unlit. The only warm light near the viewer is the flame under the hood, which lights a few paces of frosted grass in front of the figure and leaves the figure itself dark. Below, about a mile off, a cold quick river runs across the picture with a worn track beside it and a crossing of set stones. Above the stones, far and small, a cluster of stone houses with a low wall and one gate, with smoke rising straight up from several roofs. Near the crossing, outside the wall, one window is lit, a single point of gold in the dusk. Walled fields in stubble on the valley floor, and stone walls running far up both hillsides. Dark ridges close the valley on both sides. Between the figure and the river a faint straight line shows under the turf. The first stars are out. The lit window, tiny beside the dark valley, gives the scale.
